summary: American pulp writer L. Ron Hubbard invented a heroic past, launched Dianetics in 1950 and turned it into the Church of Scientology, then ruled a fleet of followers at sea from 1967 to 1975 through punishments, paranoia and fear.

evidence.note: 1934 pulp-magazine boom starts his writing career, covered at length
1975 he comes ashore in Florida; series stops here, his last years are summarised
churches incorporated in New Jersey 1953 and California 1954; Scientology recast as a religion
Dianetics sold as a cure for psychosomatic ills, even cancer and diabetes
speed-and-vitamin mix given to followers; later sauna/vitamin rehab regimes linked to deaths
after WWII he spends years exaggerating injuries to the VA for disability money
takes infant daughter from her mother and leaves her with strangers during divorce fight
flies to Havana with the baby and writes a Dianetics sequel there
fleet assembles in the Canary Islands; later sails to Valencia
fleet bases at Corfu under the Greek junta; UK bars him from entry the same day
Morocco courted as a headquarters until a failed coup forces the fleet out
small boy confined in the chain locker for two days; teen messengers wield punishment power

notes: Source .txt transcripts carry only a 00:00:00 stamp; times come from the episodes' SRT files. Main span 1950 (Dianetics) to 1986 (death), per the encyclopedia test and the reviewer; covered span is his whole life. GB = English manor, UK ban, Royal Scotman. Content warnings: Susan Meister suicide (p3 00:45:02) and a child-confinement account. Not taken: military-officer (WWII Navy segment is comic) and quack-fake-healer. domestic-abuse: wife kidnapped and strangled (p2 ~00:23-00:33, ~10 min).
